bringItHome: Wages are what your work earns — the pay owed, rendered by the record. ‘The wages of sin is death’: death is not an arbitrary sentence but the pay sin’s labor earns. And the sharp contrast in that verse is the point: sin pays a wage, but eternal life is a gift, not a wage — unearned.

courtroomRoles.does: receives the wage his labor earned, good or ill.
renders the due according to the record.
the exact pay owed for the work done.

47.lead: To walk is to conduct one’s whole manner of life by the covenant — the daily, ongoing practice of the law, one’s entire course of conduct. “Walk in all the ways which Yahuah your Elohim hath commanded you” (Deuteronomy 5:33); “Enoch walked with Elohim” (Genesis 5:24). Halak is the metaphor for the lived-out life: not an isolated act but the direction and pattern of one’s steps. To walk in the law is to live it habitually, step by step, day by day. This is the covenant not as theory but as daily practice — the whole conduct of life ordered by the terms. To walk is how one lives out the standing one has been given.

root.sense: to walk, to go, to conduct oneself; one’s manner and course of life

47.courtroomWord: A conduct term — the whole ongoing manner of life, lived by the covenant.
47.itsRole: Standing, once given, is lived out — and to walk is that living: the daily, habitual conduct ordered by the covenant. Halak is the whole course of life, not an isolated act. ‘Walk in all the ways Yahuah commanded’; ‘Enoch walked with Elohim.’ To walk in the law is to practice it step by step, the covenant as daily life. The walk is how the acquitted live out their standing — the terms kept not once but as one’s whole manner of life.

proofTexts.text: Walk in all the ways which Yahuah your Elohim hath commanded you.
proofTexts.note: The covenant as course of life.

proofTexts.text: Enoch walked with Elohim.
proofTexts.note: The whole life ordered toward Him.

proofTexts.text: To walk humbly with thy Elohim.
proofTexts.note: The manner of the covenant life.

proofTexts.text: Ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked.

plainTerms: To walk is to conduct your whole manner of life by the covenant — the daily, ongoing practice of the law, not an isolated act. ‘Walk in all the ways Yahuah commanded’; ‘Enoch walked with Elohim.’ To walk in the law is to live it step by step. The walk is how you live out the standing you’ve been given.
bringItHome: ‘Walk’ is the Bible’s word for how you live — the whole direction and pattern of your steps, day after day. ‘Enoch walked with Elohim.’ To walk in the law is not a single act but a manner of life: the covenant practiced habitually. It is how the acquitted live out the standing they were given — step by step.

courtroomRoles.does: lives out his standing by the covenant, day by day.
in whose ways the walk is ordered.
the path the walk follows.

66.lead: The widow is a protected legal class — named, alongside the orphan and the stranger, as one to whom the law owes special guardianship. “Ye shall not afflict any widow, or fatherless child” (Exodus 22:22); “he doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow” (Deuteronomy 10:18). The almanah, having lost her legal protector, is placed under the special protection of the law and of Yahuah Himself, who names Himself her defender. To harm the widow is to draw the court’s particular wrath; to defend her is to do the justice the law requires. The widow’s status is a legal category the covenant singles out for guardianship — the vulnerable made a special charge of the court.

root.sense: a widow; a protected legal class under special guardianship

66.courtroomWord: A protected-class term — the vulnerable made a special charge of the court.
66.itsRole: The law singles out the defenseless for guardianship, and the widow is chief among them — named with the orphan and the stranger as those the court especially protects. Having lost her legal protector, the almanah is placed under Yahuah’s own defense; He executes the judgment of the widow. To afflict her draws the court’s wrath; to defend her is required justice. The widow’s status is a legal category the covenant guards — the vulnerable made the court’s particular charge.

proofTexts.text: Ye shall not afflict any widow, or fatherless child.
He doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow.
A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows.
To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction.
proofTexts.note: The duty toward the protected class.

plainTerms: The widow is a protected legal class — named with the orphan and the stranger as those the law owes special guardianship. Having lost her legal protector, she is placed under Yahuah’s own defense: He ‘executes the judgment of the widow.’ To harm her draws the court’s wrath; to defend her is required justice. Her status is a category the covenant singles out for protection.
bringItHome: The widow, the orphan, and the stranger are named again and again as the law’s special charge — the vulnerable the court particularly guards. Having lost her protector, the widow is placed under Yahuah’s own defense; He calls Himself ‘a judge of the widows.’ To afflict her is to provoke the court; to defend her is the justice the law requires.

courtroomRoles.does: the vulnerable placed under special guardianship.
who executes the judgment of the widow.
required to protect, forbidden to afflict her.

7.lead: A witness is one whose testimony establishes a matter in court — the sworn source of evidence on which a case is decided. Torah builds its evidentiary law on the witness: “at the mouth of two witnesses, or three witnesses, shall the matter be established” (Deuteronomy 19:15); a single witness could not convict. The ed is the one who saw and testifies, whose corroborated word carries legal weight. A false witness was gravely punished, for he corrupts the very basis of judgment. To be a witness is to hold the responsibility of establishing truth before the court — the testimony that, corroborated, decides the case. The whole trial rests on the reliability of witnesses.

root.sense: a witness; one who testifies, whose corroborated word establishes a matter

sharesRoot.note: Eduth (the testimony) is from ed (the witness): the witness gives the testimony, and the deposited testimony is the covenant’s standing witness.

7.courtroomWord: An evidence term — the sworn source whose corroborated testimony establishes a matter.
7.itsRole: A case is decided on testimony, and the witness is its source — the one who saw and testifies, whose word, corroborated, establishes the matter. Torah requires two or three: one witness cannot convict. The false witness is gravely punished, for he corrupts judgment at its root. To be a witness is to bear the responsibility of establishing truth before the bench. The whole trial rests on the reliability of the witnesses — the matter stands or falls on their testimony.

proofTexts.text: At the mouth of two witnesses, or... three witnesses, shall the matter be established.
At the mouth of two witnesses... shall he... be put to death; but... not... one witness.
Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.
Then shall ye do unto him, as he had thought to have done unto his brother.

plainTerms: A witness is one whose testimony establishes a matter in court — the sworn source of evidence on which a case is decided. Torah requires two or three: one witness could not convict. A false witness was gravely punished, because he corrupts judgment itself. To be a witness is to bear the responsibility of establishing truth before the bench.
bringItHome: The whole trial rests on witnesses — those who saw and testify, whose corroborated word decides the case. Torah is strict: ‘two or three witnesses,’ never one, and a false witness bore the very penalty he sought to inflict. To be a witness is to hold the truth of the matter in your testimony — the case stands or falls on it.

courtroomRoles.does: testifies to establish the matter before the court.
who requires corroboration and punishes the false witness.
established at the mouth of two or three witnesses.

111.lead: Wrath is the judicial sentence executed — the settled, righteous response of the court against sin, not a fit of temper. Charon is burning anger; orge is settled indignation — but in the legal frame, wrath is the penalty the just Judge renders and carries out. “The wrath of Yahuah” against sin is not capricious rage but the lawful consequence of breach, measured and deserved. “Ye were the children of wrath” (Ephesians 2:3) names a legal liability to sentence. Wrath is not the Judge losing control but the Judge doing justice — the sentence against sin executed. It is the court’s righteous verdict rendered against what the law condemns.

root.sense: burning anger, heat of anger
settled wrath, judicial indignation

111.courtroomWord: A sentence term — the righteous judicial penalty executed against sin.
111.itsRole: Against real wrong, the just court renders a sentence, and wrath is that sentence executed — not temper but righteous requital. Charon and orge, in the legal frame, are the measured, deserved response of the Judge to breach. ‘Children of wrath’ names a liability to sentence. Wrath is the Judge doing justice, not losing control — the lawful consequence of sin, rendered and carried out. It is the court’s righteous verdict against what the law condemns.

proofTexts.text: Were by nature the children of wrath.
Treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath... of the righteous judgment of Elohim.
Yahuah... reserveth wrath for his enemies.
We shall be saved from wrath through him.
proofTexts.note: The sentence one is delivered from.

plainTerms: Wrath is the judicial sentence executed — the settled, righteous response of the court against sin, not a fit of temper. ‘The wrath of Yahuah’ is the lawful consequence of breach, measured and deserved. ‘Children of wrath’ names a liability to sentence. Wrath is the Judge doing justice, not losing control — the verdict against sin carried out.
bringItHome: Wrath, in Scripture, is not the Judge losing His temper — it is the Judge carrying out justice: the settled, deserved sentence against sin. ‘Children of wrath’ describes a legal liability to that sentence. It is measured and righteous, the lawful consequence of breach. And the good news is framed against it: ‘saved from wrath through him.’

courtroomRoles.does: renders the righteous sentence against sin.
liable to the sentence the breach incurs.
through whom one is saved from the wrath to come.

32.lead: To write is to enter a matter into the permanent record — to inscribe it as binding, documented, and enforceable. In the covenant, what is written is what stands: “these words... write them upon the posts of thy house” (Deuteronomy 6:9); the names written in the book of life (Revelation 20:15). Kathab is the act of committing to the record — a decree written cannot be casually revoked (Esther 8:8: what is written in the king’s name ‘may no man reverse’). To write is to make a thing legally documentary: the law written to be kept, the names written to be recognized, the decree written to stand. The written record is the court’s binding memory.

root.sense: to write, to inscribe, to record; to enter into the permanent record

32.courtroomWord: A record term — to enter a matter permanently and bindingly into the record.
32.itsRole: What is committed to writing stands, and to write is that committing — the matter entered permanently, documented, enforceable. The law is written to be kept; the names are written to be recognized; the decree, once written in the king’s name, may no man reverse. Kathab makes a thing legally documentary. To write is to fix a matter in the record so it binds and endures — the court’s permanent, enforceable memory.

proofTexts.text: Thou shalt write them upon the posts of thy house, and on thy gates.
proofTexts.note: The terms committed to the record.

proofTexts.text: Written with the finger of Elohim.
Written in the king’s name... may no man reverse.
proofTexts.note: The written decree binding and irrevocable.

proofTexts.text: Whosoever was not found written in the book of life.
proofTexts.note: The names entered on the record.

plainTerms: To write is to enter a matter into the permanent record — to inscribe it as binding and enforceable. What is written stands: the law written to be kept, the names written in the book of life, the decree that ‘may no man reverse.’ Kathab makes a thing legally documentary. The written record is the court’s binding memory.
bringItHome: In the ancient world, once a decree was written in the king’s name, ‘no man could reverse’ it — writing made it binding and permanent. That is kathab: entering a matter into the record so it stands. The law is written to be kept; the names are written to be recognized. The written record is the court’s memory, and it endures.

courtroomRoles.does: writes the law and the names into the record.
the law, the decree, the names, entered to stand.
whose binding memory the written record is.
